hyperedges.label: One Markdown reader serving preview, hover and fences
A tab is not always a buffer: the tab model

nodes.label: Draws the app icon and builds assets/lithe.icns. Pure stdlib: writes a PNG by…
nodes.norm_label: draws the app icon and builds assets/lithe.icns. pure stdlib: writes a png by...

nodes.label: Per-pixel coverage for a rounded square, 4x supersampled on corners.
nodes.norm_label: per-pixel coverage for a rounded square, 4x supersampled on corners.

nodes.label: git CLI for writes
nodes.rationale: Staging, committing, init and blame shell out: these are one-off actions a person asks for and git is the reference implementation.

nodes.label: gitoxide (gix) for reads
nodes.rationale: HEAD blobs and line diff in-process, so the gutter and the diff against HEAD never spawn anything; the diff is recomputed only when the file or its revision changes.

nodes.label: Preview and image decoder check the tab in front is a file
nodes.norm_label: preview and image decoder check the tab in front is a file
nodes.rationale: Both work off the active buffer and a diff tab has one, so without the check, diffing a Markdown file left a rendered preview behind it and diffing a PNG drew the picture over the diff.

nodes.label: A commit's diff outlives the panel that opened it
nodes.norm_label: a commit's diff outlives the panel that opened it
nodes.rationale: A commit diff carries no buffer, so hiding it removes the tab outright rather than handing a file back; a tab outlives the thing that opened it, which is most of what being a tab means.

nodes.label: diff_frame gives drawing and hit-testing one geometry
nodes.norm_label: diff_frame gives drawing and hit-testing one geometry
nodes.rationale: An editable diff is a mapping rather than a second editor: a diff row carries the line number it shows and the buffer's cursor is measured in the same line numbers, which is enough to place the caret. One shared geometry, because an editable diff means a click has to land on the character it looks like it landed on.

nodes.label: A working file's diff carries the buffer and takes over its tab
nodes.norm_label: a working file's diff carries the buffer and takes over its tab
nodes.rationale: Both follow from the diff's right-hand column being that buffer: two tabs would mean two undo histories for one file, and a diff that pointed at a tab would have to be put back together every time focus moved. It also retires the workaround where the diff closed on a tab switch because its keystrokes would otherwise go to whatever buffer was now in front.

nodes.label: Workspace holds Vec<Tab> and active() returns Option<&Editor>
nodes.norm_label: workspace holds vec<tab> and active() returns option<&editor>
nodes.rationale: A tab is a file, a diff, or the settings page, and None for a tab that is not editing anything is the same answer an empty workspace already gave - which is the reason every call site already handled it, and what kept this from touching the hundred places that ask for the active buffer.

nodes.label: Commit diff is read only
nodes.rationale: A diff opened from History has no buffer behind it, so it says read only and means it, and clicking through a history reuses one tab rather than leaving one per commit.

nodes.label: Editable side-by-side diff
nodes.rationale: Side by side by default because two columns is what a diff looks like everywhere else. Its right-hand column is the buffer, read from the buffer rather than from disk so an edit shows up as it is typed; it opens in that file's own tab marked with a plus-minus because the diff and the buffer are one thing.

nodes.label: Git splits by direction
nodes.rationale: Reads are gitoxide because the gutter runs on every frame and must never stall on a subprocess. Writes shell out to git: gix 0.88 exposes commit() but no way to turn an index into a tree, so committing through it would mean building tree objects and moving refs by hand, and a bug there costs someone their work where a bug in the gutter costs a redraw. The tests check the result by asking git log rather than asking ourselves.

nodes.label: Initialize Repository
nodes.rationale: Offered instead of an empty list of changes, which reads as 'nothing has changed'. It shells out to git init, so the result is the repository git would have made: its hooks, its default branch name, its templates.

nodes.label: Single-click preview tab
nodes.rationale: Clicking a file in the tree opens it in a preview tab drawn dimmer, and the next single click reuses that slot, so browsing twenty files leaves one tab rather than twenty. Double-clicking it, or typing in it, makes it permanent.

nodes.label: Source control panel (changes and history)
nodes.rationale: changes stages and unstages, history lists recent commits. git status runs when something could have changed it, not every frame. Clicking a file shows its unified diff against HEAD with long unchanged runs elided; clicking again opens it for editing.

nodes.label: A tab is not always a file
nodes.norm_label: a tab is not always a file
nodes.rationale: Settings and diffs are things you open, look at and close, which is what a tab is for. As modes drawn over the editor they hid the file you were working on and the only way back was the shortcut that opened them; there is only ever one settings tab however many times you ask.

nodes.label: View File History (--follow)
nodes.rationale: Narrows the history tab to the commits that touched one file, with --follow so a rename does not cut it short; clicking the History tab widens it back to the project.

nodes.label: The settings file tolerates unknown keys
nodes.norm_label: the settings file tolerates unknown keys
nodes.rationale: deny_unknown_fields was right while the set only grew; the first time a key was retired it took every other preference in the file down with it, because the whole parse failed and fell back to defaults. Unknown keys are now logged and ignored, which still catches a typo without punishing history.

nodes.label: settings.toml records only changes
nodes.rationale: Writing every value would freeze the defaults at the moment the file was first written: toggling one preference would record all the others as though they had been decided, and changing a default afterwards could never reach anyone who had the file. A malformed file falls back to defaults rather than refusing to start.

nodes.label: UTF-16 column counting
nodes.rationale: LSP counts columns in UTF-16 code units, which is tested round-trip through emoji and CJK.

nodes.label: Awaiting carries the request's own arguments
nodes.norm_label: awaiting carries the request's own arguments
nodes.rationale: A language-server reply is only meaningful next to the question, so Awaiting carries the name a rename asked for and the buffer revision a formatting reply has to match. A reply that arrives after the buffer has moved on is dropped rather than applied to text it does not describe.

nodes.label: Lsp::follow_up for two-step requests
nodes.rationale: A call hierarchy has to name the symbol before it can ask who calls it, and a code action may arrive without the edits it implies, so the second request is issued from the first one's reply. follow_up takes no document position, because by then the question is about something the server already named.

nodes.label: Whole-document LSP sync
nodes.rationale: Coalesced to one send per frame. Incremental sync would send less but has to agree with the server about UTF-16 ranges on every edit, and a single disagreement desynchronises it silently for the rest of the session.

nodes.label: FileBlame keeps git blame --porcelain's shape
nodes.rationale: Line blame reads the whole file once, not a line at a time: the annotation follows the cursor, so a subprocess per line would mean one per keypress on the way down a file - invariant 1 in everything but name. git blame --porcelain already sends a commit's details only the first time its sha appears, so FileBlame stores commits once and an index per line.

nodes.label: Line blame (cmd+shift+B)
nodes.rationale: One git blame per file, not per line: the annotation follows the caret and spawning a subprocess every time you press Down is not something this editor is allowed to do. Commits are stored once and referenced per line, so a ten-thousand-line file is forty kilobytes rather than ten thousand strings. A modified buffer says 'unsaved changes', because blame reads the file on disk and a confident wrong name is worse than none.

nodes.label: Measured, not asserted
nodes.rationale: macOS 27 / Apple M5 release figures: 0.000% idle CPU, 13 us of document work per frame independent of file size, a 143 MB 3M-line file open in 0.05 s, 11.8 ms worst-case fuzzy keystroke over 200,000 paths, 0.26 ms mean keystroke reparse. The floor is the platform's: 63 MB of AppKit before a line of our code runs, where Electron-based editors idle between 500 MB and 1 GB.

nodes.label: Measured memory baseline
nodes.rationale: 63 MB AppKit before a line of our code runs, 10 MB for the window, 3 MB for wgpu, 11 MB for the font and atlas stack. The floor is AppKit's, not ours, and is not reducible from inside the process; the same editor as a terminal UI would idle around 10 MB, against 500 MB to 1 GB for a mainstream Electron editor.

nodes.label: Invariant 3: no index of our own
nodes.norm_label: invariant 3: no index of our own
nodes.rationale: We never walk, parse, or cache the whole project. Symbols come from the language server; text search streams through ripgrep's engine and keeps only the matches on screen. This is the single biggest reason mainstream editors idle at 1GB and we do not.

nodes.label: Invariant 6: nothing is loaded until opened
nodes.norm_label: invariant 6: nothing is loaded until opened
nodes.rationale: Workspace open reads the directory listing of the root. Not the files, not the git objects, not the tree.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable performance invariants
nodes.rationale: These are the reason the project exists. Every feature must respect them, and a feature that cannot is cut rather than accommodated.

nodes.label: The document is fully resident at 1.15x
nodes.norm_label: the document is fully resident at 1.15x
nodes.rationale: What viewport-bounded layout does not buy, and an earlier draft of this file wrongly claimed it did: a 143 MB file is 164 MB of rope. Only the viewport is shaped - it is not the case that only the viewport is loaded.

nodes.label: Invariant 2: lay out only what is visible
nodes.norm_label: invariant 2: lay out only what is visible
nodes.rationale: Shaping and drawing are proportional to the viewport, never to the document: pulling the ~60 lines a frame needs out of the rope costs 13 us whether the file holds 60 lines or three million.

nodes.label: Virtual buffer over a memory map (unearned)
nodes.norm_label: virtual buffer over a memory map (unearned)
nodes.rationale: Making only-the-viewport-loaded true needs a virtual buffer over a memory map, which is a real project and not a milestone we have earned yet; it is also the only way to reduce the rope's 1.15x.

nodes.label: Three design invariants
nodes.rationale: Redraw only on damage, lay out only what is visible, no index of our own - stated in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md as the invariants every feature has to respect.

nodes.label: Fuzzy open (cmd+P)
nodes.rationale: Keeps paths and never file contents, and only builds that list when you first press cmd+P. This is the main reason mainstream editors idle at a gigabyte and this one does not.

nodes.label: Search on ripgrep's engine
nodes.rationale: Uses ripgrep's own grep-regex and grep-searcher so in-buffer find means exactly what project search means: one pattern syntax, one set of case rules. Project search streams, the previous worker is cancelled when you retype, and the result set is capped because a result list is the closest thing to an index we keep.

nodes.label: Viewport-bounded highlight query
nodes.rationale: The highlight query is restricted to the visible byte range, so colouring a three-million-line file costs what colouring a short one does - measured at 97 us per frame.

nodes.label: line_spans is the one definition of the lines a cursor is on
nodes.norm_label: line_spans is the one definition of the lines a cursor is on
nodes.rationale: It merges overlaps and decides that a selection ending exactly at a line start has not reached into that line. Delete, duplicate, move and comment all share it, so they cannot disagree about what the current line is when a selection spans three of them.

nodes.label: move_lines takes one cursor only
nodes.rationale: Deliberately narrower than the other multi-cursor commands: with several cursors the blocks can meet in the middle and the result is nobody's idea of a swap.

nodes.label: toggle_comment makes one decision for the whole block
nodes.norm_label: toggle_comment makes one decision for the whole block
nodes.rationale: If every line is commented it uncomments, else it comments all of it - because line by line turns a half-commented block into its own inverse, which is never what was meant.

nodes.label: Glyph atlas
nodes.rationale: A single-channel texture holding rasterised glyphs keyed by char, face and size; 94 rasterised ASCII glyphs and the font system are the 11 MB of baseline that is actually ours.

nodes.label: swash glyph rasterization
nodes.rationale: Using cosmic-text's swash backend gives real hinting and font fallback without owning a font stack.

nodes.label: ASCII fast path
nodes.rationale: A code editor is overwhelmingly a monospace ASCII grid, and exploiting that is most of the performance story: the printable ASCII range is rasterized once into the atlas, and drawing a screenful is filling an instance buffer with (cell_x, cell_y, glyph_index, fg, bg) and issuing one draw - no shaping, no per-line layout, no allocation.

nodes.label: Invariant 4: one draw call for the text plane
nodes.norm_label: invariant 4: one draw call for the text plane
nodes.rationale: The editor body is a character grid, so the whole screen is one instanced quad draw against one glyph atlas. Panels are the same primitive, not a widget tree.

nodes.label: Size::{Body, Large, Huge} instead of a number
nodes.norm_label: size::{body, large, huge} instead of a number
nodes.rationale: A uniform grid is what lets a screenful of text cost one instance per cell, so the atlas does not take a number: it takes an enum, measures each size on first use, and caches glyphs under (char, face, size). A heading then occupies two grid rows rather than a fractional height, which keeps the preview's model - a line is a scroll step, and it sits on the grid.

nodes.label: cosmic-text shaping slow path
nodes.rationale: CJK, emoji, combining marks and RTL go through full cosmic-text shaping and the shaped result is cached per unique run: rare in source code, correct when it happens.

nodes.label: Fractional scrolling
nodes.rationale: Fractional rather than line-by-line, because a trackpad sends pixel deltas and rounding each one to a whole line is what makes scrolling feel like it is catching.

nodes.label: LITHE_TRACE event logging
nodes.rationale: Logs every window event, which is what makes the redraw-on-damage invariant measurable rather than asserted.

nodes.label: --snapshot frame capture
nodes.rationale: Renders one frame to raw RGBA, optionally with an overlay such as the picker up, so a frame can be inspected outside a live window.

nodes.label: The one bounded timer: caret blink
nodes.norm_label: the one bounded timer: caret blink
nodes.rationale: The caret blinks for ten seconds after the last keystroke and then goes solid, so the editor blinks while you work and wakes for nothing once you stop. Anything else wanting a clock gets the same treatment - bounded, self-cancelling, and justified in this file.

nodes.label: The dwell is fenced in on every side
nodes.norm_label: the dwell is fenced in on every side
nodes.rationale: It is the one thing the editor does without being asked: only over text, only after the pointer has been still, only once per rest, and only when a server is already running. It schedules itself through the same deadline the caret blink and the autosave use, so an idle window still waits for nothing at all.

nodes.label: How to measure idle CPU
nodes.rationale: Two different mistakes both look exactly like a broken invariant: top makes the window it samples redraw and reports one to three percent of its own making, and a pointer resting over a focused window still delivers events. Use a ps CPU-time delta plus the event count over the same window: zero events with non-zero CPU is a real bug, events with CPU is the editor doing its job.

nodes.label: Invariant 1: redraw only on damage
nodes.rationale: The event loop sits in ControlFlow::Wait with no animation ticker and no continuous render loop, so an idle window costs 0% CPU. If a feature needs a steady frame clock, it is the feature that is wrong.

nodes.label: Hover (400ms dwell, cmd+I)
nodes.rationale: The answer is drawn as a small document because a server sends Markdown, and a signature arrives as a highlighted code block. Nothing is asked unless a server for that language is already running: resting a pointer must not start a process.

nodes.label: Offscreen pixel tests
nodes.rationale: A hand-rolled text renderer fails in ways a type checker cannot see, so the renderer can draw to an offscreen texture and the tests read the pixels back. The render tests skip rather than fail where there is no GPU.

nodes.label: Markdown preview reader
nodes.rationale: Headings, paragraphs, emphasis, code, all three link kinds, lists, checkboxes, quotes, rules, pipe tables, hidden YAML front matter and inline HTML. One font at one size, so structure is carried by weight and colour; fenced code is highlighted by the editor's own tree-sitter grammars, and a fence naming an uninstalled language stays plain rather than being coloured by a guess.

nodes.label: initialize declares hover.contentFormat Markdown
nodes.rationale: The hover popup is the Markdown preview in a box, and without hover.contentFormat a server must send plaintext - clangd did, so a signature arrived as a flat string with nothing to colour. The reply is kept as written rather than flattened to one line, which is what the status bar used to need.

nodes.label: The HTML preview is gone
nodes.rationale: A reader that understands the structural tags but no stylesheet, script or layout renders a document the way nothing on the web would, and 'roughly a browser' is a worse promise than no promise. Inline HTML inside Markdown stayed, because there it is part of the Markdown rather than a claim to render a page.

nodes.label: Void elements are checked before hidden tags
nodes.norm_label: void elements are checked before hidden tags
nodes.rationale: An HTML void element must never be in the hidden-tag set. <meta> was, and since nothing ever closes it, every page with a charset declaration rendered as a blank screen; the two lists are now separate and the void one is checked first.

nodes.label: A run boundary is part of a word, not a break
nodes.norm_label: a run boundary is part of a word, not a break
nodes.rationale: The reader emits one run per style, so [link](x). is three runs and one word; splitting each run on its own spaces and rejoining with a single space put a gap before every full stop that followed a link. Words are built across runs first, then laid out.

nodes.label: HTML has no preview
nodes.rationale: It had one and it was never what anyone wanted: a reader that understands the structural tags but no stylesheet, script or layout shows a document nothing on the web would render that way. Inline HTML inside Markdown is still read.

nodes.label: Images named, not drawn, in Markdown
nodes.norm_label: images named, not drawn, in markdown
nodes.rationale: A picture inside flowed text would mean laying out rows of unequal height around it, and for the badges at the top of a README the name is all there was to say.

nodes.label: Preview for Markdown, SVG and images
nodes.norm_label: preview for markdown, svg and images
nodes.rationale: Each kind opens either rendered or as its source and remembers which you chose; Markdown defaults to its source, SVG and images to the picture. A file that is not text opens as an image or a note saying so, and is never written back over.

nodes.label: SVG has its own preview switch
nodes.norm_label: svg has its own preview switch
nodes.rationale: SVG is the one picture format that is also a text file worth editing: turning its preview off shows the markup, while doing the same to a PNG would show an empty buffer.

nodes.label: Unknown HTML tags left as written
nodes.norm_label: unknown html tags left as written
nodes.rationale: Left as written rather than dropped, because Vec<T> in prose is commoner in a code editor's README than hand-written HTML.

nodes.label: Crate layout
nodes.rationale: Split for compile-time isolation and to keep editing logic pure: core has no I/O, no GPU and no async, and each later crate stays a leaf so touching cursor logic never recompiles wgpu.

nodes.label: A throwaway Syntax per fence
nodes.rationale: Nothing is kept: a fence is tens of lines, the result is cached with the rendered preview, and a parser per code block would cost more than re-running this on the edit that invalidates it.

nodes.label: File tree context menu
nodes.rationale: New File/Folder, Reveal in Finder, Open in Default App or Terminal, Cut/Copy/Duplicate/Paste, Undo/Redo, Copy Path, Rename, Move to Trash, Delete. Right-clicking empty space acts on the project root.

nodes.label: The tree's inline edit row is a real row
nodes.norm_label: the tree's inline edit row is a real row
nodes.rationale: Inserted into rows where the result will appear, so drawing and hit-testing need no notion of it; the only place that knows is the one line that draws its label.

nodes.label: Rename edits open buffers and closed files differently
nodes.norm_label: rename edits open buffers and closed files differently
nodes.rationale: Opening every touched file as a tab would be tidier for undo and worse to use: a rename across forty files would leave forty tabs.

nodes.label: References and call lists fill the search panel
nodes.norm_label: references and call lists fill the search panel
nodes.rationale: Find All References and the two call lists reuse the search panel so they scroll and click through the same way a project search does.

nodes.label: Copy Permalink to Line
nodes.rationale: Builds a link to the current commit on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, and says it cannot rather than guessing at an unknown host.

nodes.label: File clipboard with its own undo
nodes.norm_label: file clipboard with its own undo
nodes.rationale: The path also goes on the system clipboard so it is not a black hole. Undo and Redo take back what the menu did to the filesystem; Move to Trash is recoverable and is what Undo reverses, while Delete is not, so it is the one entry that asks first.

nodes.label: In-place naming in the tree
nodes.rationale: New File, New Folder and Rename are typed on the row where the result will appear. A name is a name: one containing a path separator is refused rather than silently writing somewhere else, and an existing file is never overwritten.

nodes.label: Rename Symbol
nodes.rationale: Asks for the new name, then applies the server's workspace edit - to open buffers as an undoable change, and to closed files directly on disk.

nodes.label: Context menus built per click
nodes.rationale: Two menus, built per click from what is actually actionable - an entry that would quietly do nothing is not offered. LSP entries need a server for the language; git entries need the project to be a repository.

nodes.label: Landing page
nodes.rationale: Launched with no argument: New buffer, Open file, Open folder, New window, and recently opened projects. Every row is clickable, and the status-bar panel toggles stay clickable here because that is when you are most likely to reach for one.

nodes.label: Full-area pages are hit-tested where the text area is
nodes.norm_label: full-area pages are hit-tested where the text area is
nodes.rationale: Not before the chrome: testing the settings page first meant it returned 'nothing here' for every click outside its own switches, which swallowed the sidebar and, once it became a tab, the click on its own tab. The landing page had the same shape and the same fix.

nodes.label: Temp-file-and-rename save
nodes.rationale: Saving goes through a temp file and a rename so an interrupted write cannot truncate your code; closing with unsaved edits asks first, in a native dialog.

nodes.label: Autosave
nodes.rationale: Writes a modified buffer back after a pause in typing and when the window loses focus. Only buffers that have a path: inventing a filename for a scratch buffer would be worse than leaving it unsaved. It goes through the same temp-file-and-rename path a manual save does.

nodes.label: Independent windows sharing one GPU device
nodes.norm_label: independent windows sharing one gpu device
nodes.rationale: Each window owns its project root, open buffers and file tree, so a second window can sit on a different repository. They share one wgpu device and one rasterised glyph atlas, which is why a second window costs five megabytes rather than twenty - the font system behind the atlas is eight on its own.

nodes.label: Opening a folder replaces the project
nodes.norm_label: opening a folder replaces the project
nodes.rationale: Rather than merging into it: two projects' files in one tree is never what was meant.

nodes.label: Recent projects file
nodes.rationale: One plain text file, one absolute path per line, under Application Support or XDG_CONFIG_HOME. No database, nothing to migrate, and you can edit it in the editor. Writing it re-reads first and merges, since several windows each hold their own copy and a stale write would drop whatever another added.

nodes.label: Milestones M1-M7
nodes.rationale: Each one ends at something usable, not a demo; since M7: the four goto requests, references, call hierarchy, rename, formatting, code actions with codeAction/resolve, context menus, in-place naming and a file clipboard with its own undo stack.

nodes.label: lithe
nodes.rationale: A bare-bones code editor in Rust, local only: no account, no telemetry, no network, no LLM. Code editing, LSP, search, version control, and nothing else.

nodes.label: Roadmap M1-M7 (all done)
nodes.rationale: the frame, the editor, files, syntax, search, lsp, vcs - each milestone ends at something usable.

nodes.label: Mac app bundle (scripts/bundle.sh)
nodes.rationale: A bare binary run from a terminal is only half an app to macOS: unreliable menu bar, executable name in the Dock, no icon. The bundle adds an Info.plist, a generated icon and an ad-hoc signature, which is what makes the native menu behave.

nodes.label: Native menu bar (File, Edit, Go, View)
nodes.norm_label: native menu bar (file, edit, go, view)
nodes.rationale: Exists so the shortcuts are discoverable rather than folklore; Open File, Open Folder and Save As use the system dialogs.

nodes.label: Two render primitives: rect and text
nodes.norm_label: two render primitives: rect and text
nodes.rationale: Editor body, gutter, file tree, command palette, search results and status bar are all the same two calls at different coordinates - one instanced draw per frame against one glyph atlas. There is no widget tree.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled wgpu text renderer
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a UI toolkit because a code editor is a character grid and that fact is worth exploiting.

nodes.label: tree-sitter grammars, nine languages
nodes.rationale: Rust, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, Python, Go, C, JSON and TOML; the nine grammars are about 6 MB of the 12 MB stripped binary.

nodes.label: Adding a language is a dependency and a row
nodes.norm_label: adding a language is a dependency and a row
nodes.rationale: Adding one is a dependency and a row in crates/syntax/src/languages.rs - the language set is table-driven rather than wired through code paths.

nodes.label: Highlighting switched off above 2 MB
nodes.rationale: A parse tree is about 26x the source it describes, so highlighting stops above 2 MB; past that a file still opens instantly, just uncoloured.

nodes.label: Incremental parsing
nodes.rationale: An edit is described to the tree before the reparse, so a keystroke costs a fraction of a millisecond instead of re-parsing the file. The parser reads the rope in chunks and never flattens it into a String.

nodes.label: Undo discards the tree and reparses
nodes.norm_label: undo discards the tree and reparses
nodes.rationale: Rather than deriving inverse edits: ~16 ms on a 14,000-line file, fine for a keypress and visible if you hold the key down.

nodes.label: Two bounded completion signals
nodes.rationale: Trigger characters come from the server's own initialize reply rather than a list of ours, because which characters mean 'a member follows' is a fact about the language; they arrive one character at a time, which is also how a keystroke does, so > covers ->. The other signal is two characters of a word and fires once rather than once per letter. Neither signal starts a server: a keystroke must not spawn a process.

nodes.label: Invariant 5: language servers are separate, lazy and killable
nodes.norm_label: invariant 5: language servers are separate, lazy and killable
nodes.rationale: Spawned on the first buffer of that language, terminated when the last one closes. Their memory is theirs: rust-analyzer will use gigabytes and that is its business, not ours, while our own process stays in tens of megabytes.

nodes.label: Self-opening completion list
nodes.rationale: Opens on a character the server names as a trigger and after two characters of a word. One request per word, not one per keystroke: once the list is open, further typing narrows what it already has, which costs nothing and needs no round trip. Accepting one replaces the typed word rather than following it.

nodes.label: Language server lifecycle and probing
nodes.rationale: One process per language, started on the first buffer that needs it and killed on exit. A candidate that spawns and then exits within 250 ms is treated as broken and the next is tried, because being on PATH is not enough: rust-analyzer there is often a rustup proxy for a component never installed. The status bar names the state and asking a missing server names the command that installs it.

hyperedges.label: One Markdown reader serving preview, hover and fences
A tab is not always a buffer: the tab model
